Real leaders who held a line
Fictional leaders who held a line

leaders.name: Adolf Hitler
leaders.tagline: Started World War II in Europe and ran the Holocaust, the state-sponsored murder of six million Jews and millions of others.

leaders.name: Joseph Stalin
leaders.tagline: Forced collectivization and industrialization at the price of famine, and removed rivals through purges, labor camps, and executions.

leaders.name: Mao Zedong
leaders.tagline: His Great Leap Forward and Cultural Revolution brought famine and upheaval that killed tens of millions.

leaders.name: Pol Pot
leaders.tagline: Led the Khmer Rouge in a drive for an agrarian utopia that ended in genocide, forced labor, and starvation.

leaders.name: King Leopold II
leaders.tagline: Ran the Congo Free State as a private enterprise, using forced labor and terror to extract rubber and ivory.

leaders.name: Hideki Tojo
leaders.tagline: Prime Minister through most of World War II, who oversaw expansion across Asia marked by war crimes and massacres.

leaders.name: Benito Mussolini
leaders.tagline: Founded Fascism and ruled as Il Duce, dismantling democracy and tying Italy to Nazi Germany.

leaders.name: Saddam Hussein
leaders.tagline: Ruled through a police state, used chemical weapons on Kurdish civilians, and launched wars on Iran and Kuwait.

leaders.name: Talaat Pasha
leaders.tagline: Interior minister who directed the deportations and massacres of the Armenian Genocide.

leaders.name: Ranavalona I
leaders.tagline: Queen who sealed her kingdom, enforced forced labor and trial by poison, and persecuted Christians and rival groups.

leaders.name: Macbeth
leaders.tagline: A Scottish general who murdered his king to take the crown, then killed again to keep it.

leaders.name: Richard III
leaders.tagline: A scheming duke who removed every rival, even his own nephews, certain no one else had the nerve.

leaders.name: Captain Ahab
leaders.tagline: A whaling captain who bent an entire crew to his hunt for one whale.

leaders.name: Kurtz
leaders.tagline: An ivory agent who made himself ruler of a remote station in the Congo, governing through terror.

leaders.name: Dr. Moreau
leaders.source: The Island of Doctor Moreau, H. G. Wells
leaders.tagline: A scientist who rules a private island and reshapes living creatures by force.

leaders.name: The Benefactor
leaders.tagline: Ruler of the One State, who traded freedom for guaranteed happiness.

leaders.name: Creon
leaders.tagline: A king who put the law of the state above conscience and would not bend.

leaders.name: Clytemnestra
leaders.tagline: A queen who ruled in her husband's absence and killed him on his return for the daughter he sacrificed.

leaders.name: Goneril
leaders.tagline: A princess who took her father's kingdom and stripped him of his power.

leaders.name: Cao Cao
leaders.source: Romance of the Three Kingdoms, Luo Guanzhong
leaders.tagline: A warlord and chancellor willing to betray the world before it could betray him.

leaders.name: Nelson Mandela
leaders.tagline: Spent 27 years imprisoned under apartheid, then as president chose reconciliation over revenge.
leaders.flaw: Armed struggle in his earlier years included sabotage, and he later said he had been too slow to confront the AIDS crisis.

leaders.name: Abraham Lincoln
leaders.tagline: Led the nation through civil war to preserve the Union and issued the Emancipation Proclamation.
leaders.flaw: Suspended habeas corpus during the war and held views on race that he revised over time.

leaders.name: Ashoka the Great
leaders.tagline: After the Kalinga War, renounced conquest and built a state on nonviolence, welfare, and religious tolerance.
leaders.flaw: His turn to nonviolence followed a conquest that cost many lives, and his edicts are his own account of himself.

leaders.name: Cyrus the Great
leaders.tagline: Governed through cultural and religious pluralism and let exiled peoples, including the Jews in Babylon, return home.
leaders.flaw: A conqueror whose Cylinder is also a victory proclamation, so its reputation as a charter of rights is partly later legend.

leaders.name: Mahatma Gandhi
leaders.tagline: Mobilized a nation against colonial rule through satyagraha, active nonviolent resistance.
leaders.flaw: His early writings in South Africa contain racist views of Black Africans, and his views on caste and women drew lasting criticism.

leaders.name: King Sejong the Great
leaders.tagline: Gave commoners a way to read and write with the Hangul script, and advanced medicine and agriculture.
leaders.flaw: Presided over a rigidly hierarchical society and conducted military campaigns against neighboring peoples.

leaders.name: Saladin
leaders.tagline: Known in the Crusades for chivalry, granting safe passage and sparing civilians after Jerusalem fell.
leaders.flaw: Had many captured Templars and Hospitallers executed after the Battle of Hattin.

leaders.name: Eleanor Roosevelt
leaders.source: United States and the United Nations
leaders.tagline: Led the drafting and passage of the 1948 Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
leaders.flaw: Carried prejudices from her early life that she spent decades revising, and was cautious on civil rights legislation early on.

leaders.name: Elizabeth I
leaders.tagline: Held a divided, threatened kingdom together for decades through shrewd diplomacy and religious moderation, and turned back the Spanish Armada.
leaders.flaw: Her reign included harsh repression of dissent and brutal campaigns in Ireland.

leaders.name: Wangari Maathai
leaders.tagline: Founded the Green Belt Movement, planting millions of trees, and was beaten and jailed for challenging a dictatorship before winning the Nobel Peace Prize.
leaders.flaw: Her public statements about the origins of HIV drew sharp criticism.

leaders.name: King Arthur
leaders.tagline: The legendary king who gathered rival lords around a round table so that none ranked above another.

leaders.name: Penelope
leaders.tagline: Queen of Ithaca who held her household and kingdom together through years of absence, outwitting suitors who wanted her throne.

leaders.name: Henry V
leaders.tagline: A young king who led an outnumbered army by sharing its hardships, though the play also shows him threatening a besieged town.

leaders.name: Antigone
leaders.tagline: A princess who defied a king's decree to bury her brother, accepting death rather than abandon what she held right.

leaders.name: Jean Valjean
leaders.tagline: A convict turned factory owner and mayor who spends a lifetime choosing mercy and justice over his own safety.

leaders.name: Gilgamesh
leaders.tagline: A tyrant king who learns humility through loss and returns to rule his city with wisdom.

leaders.name: Hua Mulan
leaders.tagline: A woman who took her aged father's place in the army and served through years of war, then declined every honor to go home.

leaders.name: Sundiata Keita
leaders.tagline: A prince who overcame exile to unite the peoples of West Africa and found the Mali Empire.

leaders.name: Robin Hood
leaders.tagline: An outlaw leader who took from the corrupt and powerful to give to the poor, loyal to a rightful king.

leaders.name: Prospero
leaders.tagline: A deposed duke with total power over his enemies who chooses forgiveness over revenge and gives up his magic.
